## Summary

Wolf endorses Miles Cranmer's MPhil talk **"How to avoid AI Brain Rot"** ("a great watch") and lists favorite points:

- **Socratic AI > answer AI:** using AI to ask yourself Socratic questions instead of giving you the answer *feels* like you're learning less, but research shows you actually learn more.
- **(truncated at capture)** "ai tooling is moving so fast that…" — tweet text cut mid-sentence by the syndication API; remaining points unknown.

**Chain:** Wolf's tweet quotes Cranmer's "Here is the full talk" post → [talk video tweet](https://x.com/MilesCranmer/status/2111105654211608847), which quotes Cranmer's original announcement: *"Had fun writing this talk for our MPhil students today: 'How to avoid AI Brain Rot'. Discussing how to avoid intelligence atrophy from AI use in work and study. And how to stand out on an ever-narrowing bell curve."* The t.co links resolve to the tweets' own video/photo — no external article.

## Why it matters

- The Socratic pattern is directly deployable here: AI that *quizzes* you on captured material (Librarian study notes) instead of only summarizing — summarizing is exactly the "atrophy" Cranmer warns about.
- "Standing out on an ever-narrowing bell curve" is the same thesis as the taste/curation notes ([[2026-10-18-copyconstruct-claude-md-curated-corpus]] is the adjacent angle: curation as the scarce skill).

**Skepticism gates:**
- "Research shows" is uncited in the tweet — no paper linked. Treat as *claimed*, not verified, until the talk is watched.
- Wolf's list is second-hand and truncated at capture; the primary source is the talk itself (not yet viewed).
